page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin holds three notes: the section number "II.", "Ludi gy-mnastici corporis vel animi.", and "Arist. Eth. lib. 4. c. 8." Running head at top with page number 36. Catchword "lusu" at the lower right.

main_text.p: vitatis replebuntur pueris & puellis, ludentib. in plateis ejus. Offendatur approbatio: quia promittitur ut beneficium Dei.
Occupatio: Non defendi lasciviam vel petulantiam accidentem: quam peccatum esse, deprecatio Augustini docet.

II.Argum. II. seu II. genus ludorum licitorum: Gymnastici corporis vel animi. Ludi gy-mnastici corporis vel animi.Enumerentur aliqui additis alicubi brevissimis descriptionibus, quales fuerint vel sint: Pila: discus: saltus: cursus: cestus: Par impar: Latrunculi: Astragali five taxilli, &c.
Addantur conditiones: quibus sint liciti: 1. non sint noxii fortunis aut valetudini nostrae vel alienae. 2. sint moderati. 3. tempestivi.

Probetur sic esse licitos. 1. quia reparant vires animi laboribus fessi. Amplif. à necessario: Hominis animum requirere Arist. Eth. lib. 4. c. 8. aliquam relaxationem & oblectationem [?] ἕσης δὲ καὶ ἀναπαύσεως ἐν τῷ βίῳ, καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ Διαγωγῆς μετὰ παιδιᾶς. Et: δο-κεῖ δὲ ἡ ἀνάπαυσις καὶ ἡ παιδιὰ ἐν τῷ βίῳ εἶναι ἀ-ναγκαῖον.

p.i: Arcus & arma tua tibi sint metuenda Diana:
Si nunquam cesses tendere: mollis erit.

main_text.p: II. Quia augent & conservant valetudinem. Aristot. Eth. lib. 2. cap. 2. γυμνάσια σύμμετρα ποιεῖ καὶ αὔξει καὶ σώζει τὴν ὑγίειαν.
III. Quia juvant agilitatem, quae est utile & decorum corporis bonum.
IV. à concessione Legum. Cod. lib. 3. tit. 43. in constitutione nova Justinianus prohibito alearum

page.notes: Left margin notes are placed at the paragraphs where they stand. The Greek is copied as printed. The word after "ἕσης" and the Greek opening of the Aristotle passage are doubtful. The bracketed [?] after "oblectationem" marks the uncertain Greek lead-in. The section mark "I I." in the margin is read as II. The Argum. line also reads "I I." in print and is given as II.
